requiredFixes: Section 03 (Visual Timeline): Label 'reducing first-screen cognitive load' as interpretation, not observed fact. Evidence shows headline and nav changes, not cognitive load measurement.

Section 03 (Visual Timeline): Label 'may feel more credible to enterprise evaluators while becoming less scannable for self-serve visitors' as interpretation. No A/B test data on credibility or scannability in evidence.
Section 05 (CTA): Label 'which may create a self-selection burden' as interpretation. No user testing or conversion data supports this causal claim.

Section 06 (Lessons): Remove or label all conversion outcome claims: 'reduces initial resistance', 'may increase drop-off', 'reduce friction', 'may confuse users'. None of these have supporting data in the evidence.

Section 06 (Lessons): The entire section restates analysis from sections 04 and 05 (headline shift, nav shift, section heading audit) without converting it into new action. Rewrite to offer practical founder experiments, not restatements of the analysis already presented.

Overall concision: The self-serve→enterprise shift appears explicitly in sections 01, 03, 04, 05, and 06 (5 times). Reduce to 1-2 mentions maximum. The proof burden concept appears in sections 04 and 06 (2 times, acceptable). CTA friction direction appears in sections 05 and 06 (2 times, borderline).

Section 05: The buyer-segment microcopy suggestion is excellent. Consider adding one more CTA-specific founder test (e.g., tracking which CTA gets more engagement from organic vs paid traffic).
